Guidance & outlook: Coming to Q1 FY27, we'd like to inform you that revenue from operations recorded came in at INR 304 crores, which is up by 4.3% precisely compared to Q1 FY26.

In Q1 FY27, revenue from auto components grew by 13.5 percentage compared to Q1 FY26, amounting to INR163 crores, while revenue from bearing rings, it got declined by 6% compared with Q1 FY26, amounting to INR118 crores.
I'm not considering other income, which is up by 12% on comparing with the Q1 FY26, with the EBITDA margin at a percentage of 22.6%, which is up by 100 basis points, again, on comparing with Q1 FY26.
Growth & demand: Though this looks short of our guided growth, our order book through the quarter was healthy, and the constraint we faced was not demand.
Profit after tax grew by 22% year- on-year to INR60 crores, with PAT margin at 19.8%, again up by 290 basis points year-on-year basis.
So for a mid-teen growth, assuming 15% sort of growth if we do for this year, so it will be around INR1,300 crores.
Margins & costs: Coming to the margin side, as you must have seen, gross margins for the quarter have come up compared to fiscal '26 or on a Q1 FY26, reflecting both a favorable shift in product mix as well as disciplined raw material management and scientific production measures, cost control areas at our plant level.
The EBITDA margin, what we have recorded, is 21.5% in this particular quarter, June '26*.
The correct EBITDA Margin for the quarter is 22.6%.
Capex & expansion: Rolex Rings Limited August 06, 2026 I want to emphasize that this margin expansion came through even in a quarter where our production was constrained because of labor and certain other matters.
This is the third consecutive quarter of a year-on-year margin expansion for us, and it reflects a structural improvement in our businesses.
And since our utilization is still at 60% this year, going towards 72%, and capex figures are around INR30 crores to INR40 crores only.
Balance sheet & cash: Would like to inform you that our INR180 crores buyback of 1 crores equity shares concluded during the quarter, with the promoter group choosing not to participate so that the full benefit flowed directly to non-promoter shareholders.
As of today, we are fully debt-free and clear of all legacy CDR obligations.

Maybe, as we have recently completed the buyback of INR180 crores, apart from that, we may look for distributing dividends or maybe another round of buyback or something; that is what we might be looking for.
Risks & challenges: Rolex Rings Limited August 06, 2026 The bearing rings softness was concentrated in the industrial business or in the industrial segment, particularly in the domestic and European market, an area where we have flagged our broader industry-wide stagnancy in the past, and it reflects the same labor-driven output constraint that affected quarter too.
And it was the domestic-facing portion that saw the softness this quarter.

Buyers who had been a bit cautious and holding back through in fiscal '26, with a wait-and-watch mode as tariff uncertainty and certain adverse market factors played out, are now placing orders again with confidence.

Guidance & outlook: With duties now normalizing, we expect U.S. order flows to resume meaningfully from Q1 of current fiscal, that is FY 2027.

The 30% revenue decline we experienced in the U.S. through FY 2026 is entirely recoverable and the pace of recovery will depend on how quickly our customers rebuild their inventory pipelines and production schedules.

Rolex Rings Limited May 18, 2026 Coming to the next part of your question, that is growth for FY 2027, FY 2028, would like to inform that for fiscal 2027, what we expect as on date is maybe a mid-teen growth, 15% to 17% growth, something like that.
Growth & demand: Revenue from Europe grew by almost 25% during the year compared to previous fiscal.
Domestic revenue grew by 50% year-on-year, with both bearing rings and auto components contributing meaningfully.
The growth momentum what we built in fiscal2026 is continuing into fiscal 2027 and more than 60% of our new program, what we awarded from the customers, are from European customers only.
Margins & costs: Coming to the operating numbers, operating margins, our gross margin expanded meaningfully from 49.4% to 51.5% in fiscal 2026, reflecting the positive shift in product mix towards higher- value machine auto components and a better raw material management.

So, we are in the range of 62% to 63% of utilization of my available or achievable capacity.
Capex & expansion: At the peak of the tariff uncertainty, a major customer temporarily shut down the relevant plant entirely when duties, import tariffs moved from 3% to 53%.
Our business generated INR190 crores in our operating cash flow and spent hardly INR36 crores on capex, leaving substantial free cash for the company to deploy.
No doubt, we do have capacity -- spare capacity available, but there are certain kind of range of the products where the equipments are almost 80%, 85% capacity utilization.

The sharp escalation of U.S. import tariffs, which peaked at over 50% on our auto components, created significant headwinds in our export business, particularly in the commercial vehicle and heavy commercial vehicle segment that makes up the core of our U.S. exposure.
